purpose: Freeze the reference kernel source, configuration, and boot predicate for the ARM64 flight lab.

kernel.versionDecision: Pinned to 6.18.44 on 2026-08-10. The original Day-1 goal text named 6.18.43, but the release authority showed 6.18.44 (released 2026-08-09) as the current 6.18 longterm update; per the project rule that version decisions follow the release authority, the pin was amended before any artifact was fetched.

tarball.trustAnchor: GPG signature verification against the kernel.org stable release signing key; the sha256 below is recorded after the first signature-verified fetch.

signatureEvidence.signerIdentity: Greg Kroah-Hartman (Linux kernel stable release signing key)
signatureEvidence.keySource: hkps://keyserver.ubuntu.com (keys.openpgp.org strips user IDs and cannot serve this key)

config.baseNote: virtconfig merges arch/arm64/configs/virt.config onto defconfig; it is the virtualization-guest configuration matching the QEMU virt machine.
config.laneSplit: Kconfig evaluates compiler-capability conditions (CONFIG_HAS_LTO_CLANG, CONFIG_CFI, CONFIG_RANDSTRUCT_FULL, compiler version probes), so one shared .config cannot serve both oracle toolchains. Each lane freezes its own canonical .config; the anti-shrinkage rule applies per lane.
config.freezePolicy: Generate once per lane with that lane's toolchain, canonicalize through olddefconfig, record the raw .config bytes and their sha256 here; shrinking the config to rescue a failing gate is forbidden.

clang.toolchainProbe: CC=clang-19 LD=ld.lld-19 AR=llvm-ar-19 NM=llvm-nm-19 OBJCOPY=llvm-objcopy-19 OBJDUMP=llvm-objdump-19 STRIP=llvm-strip-19

qemu.machineNote: Never the floating 'virt' alias; dtb-randomness=off; never '-cpu max'.

lanes.name: hvf-host
lanes.role: fast local flight on the M2 Max

lanes.name: tcg-cortex-a72
lanes.role: portable conformance witness with a fixed CPU model

qemu.laneEquivalence: Both lanes must boot the same Image, but runtime state and timing are NOT claimed bit-identical across CPU models.

requirements: serial log contains the per-run nonce exactly once, injected via kernel cmdline and echoed by init
boot markers appear in the contract-defined order
shutdown is controlled (poweroff), not a panic or timeout
a replayed log from an earlier run, a fixed marker without nonce, a wrong rootfs, or a wrong nonce must all FAIL the predicate
